Winnow.built_with: Lean 4, drawn by LeanNative's generated Objective-C/UIKit shell; no Swift

engine.text: Its own, in Lean 4 (Lean/Winnow, and Lean/Secp, a secp256k1 whose field and curve arithmetic carry machine-checked proofs), in the same repository: keys, PSBTs, scripts, compact-filter sync, peer networking over Lean's libuv TCP

chain_data.text: BIP157/158 compact filters from Bitcoin peers found through the census peer list shipped with the build (its signature checked when the build is made) and DNS seeds; Advanced mode adds your own peers

third_party.text: Nobody for the everyday wallet; multisig accounts need their other signers (phones, Ledgers or keys someone sent), with no co-signing server

distribution.text: App Store, in the listing the Swift app used (com.btcswift.app); tagged builds upload to TestFlight

libraries.text: LeanNative 7ab7ec8 (its Lean framework, C shim and printed Objective-C shell) and Lean 4.35.0's runtime and standard library (libLean, libStd, libInit, libleanrt) with the toolchain's libuv and GMP; no package from a registry

prebuilt.text: None in the repository; the build links the Lean toolchain's static libraries (libLean, libStd, libInit, libleanrt, libuv, libgmp), macOS arm64 objects retargeted to iOS by LeanNative's retarget_ar.py

Winnow.patched: No patch files; the build rewrites the platform (LC_BUILD_VERSION) of Lean's macOS static libraries to iOS, which Lean does not support

BlueWallet.built_with: React Native (TypeScript) with small native modules

engine.text: Its own TypeScript (class/wallets) on bitcoinjs-lib 7 and @noble/secp256k1; chain data through a fork of the Electrum client

chain_data.text: Electrum servers: electrum1.bluewallet.io by default, a short hardcoded fallback list; any host and port can be set in Settings > Network

third_party.text: Nobody for on-chain funds. The optional LNDhub (custodial) and Ark wallet types depend on their own servers

distribution.text: App Store; builds go through TestFlight

libraries.text: bitcoinjs-lib, bip32, bip39, ecpair, @noble/secp256k1, BlueWallet forks of coinselect, rn-electrum-client, bip47, SilentPayments and slip39-js, aezeed, bolt11, payjoin-client, bc-ur (Keystone and NGRAVE), realm, react-native-keychain, @arkade-os/sdk and boltz-swap, Bugsnag.

prebuilt.text: No binaries are checked in. The build links React Native's prebuilt Hermes and React-Core-prebuilt pods, and the patched react-native-background-fetch pod vendors the npm package's TSBackgroundFetch.xcframework.

BlueWallet.patched: Four patch-package patches on npm packages: react-native-background-fetch (iOS xcframework with Catalyst), react-native-notifications (Android token), react-native-context-menu-view (Android menus), react-native-screens (iOS accessibility id; patch is for 4.27.0 while package.json pins 4.28.0). Several dependencies also come from BlueWallet forks pinned to git commits.

engine.text: gdk {version:gdk} (C++ for multisig, Rust for singlesig), linked as a prebuilt static library

chain_data.text: Singlesig: Blockstream's Electrum server, or your own in Settings. Multisig: Blockstream's backend, not replaceable

third_party.text: Nobody for singlesig. Multisig (2-of-2, 2-of-3) needs Blockstream's server to co-sign every spend

libraries.text: gdk (libwally-core, rust-bitcoin, Tor), Liquid Wallet Kit, Greenlight SDK, Firebase, Countly, Zendesk, Rive, Charts, SwiftCBOR, AsyncBluetooth

Green.bitcoin_library_not_counted: libwally-core, rust-bitcoin, rust-elements (inside the prebuilt gdk)

prebuilt.text: gdk static library (libgreen_gdk_full.a) from Blockstream's release tarballs, checked against pinned SHA-256 sums; Google's grpc-binary and abseil-cpp-binary packages

Green.patched: Countly's iOS SDK comes from a fork (angelix/countly-sdk-ios 23.6.1-ave). gdk's own build patches libevent and bc-ur, outside the app.

Muun.built_with: Swift (UIKit) with a Go library, libwallet

engine.text: libwallet, Muun's own Go library in the same repository: keys, 2-of-2 and MuSig2 signing, addresses, fees. Muun's server holds the second key

chain_data.text: Muun's own server (Houston API): history, spendable coins, fees and block height. The person cannot change it

third_party.text: Muun's server must co-sign every spend. Without it the person needs the Emergency Kit, the Recovery Code and Muun's separate Recovery Tool

Muun.distribution: App Store, per its fastlane release lane

libraries.text: Swift: Firebase (Analytics, Crashlytics, Messaging), GoogleSignIn and Google Drive API, GRDB.swift, RxSwift, Dip, grpc-swift, Lottie. Go: btcd, lnd (lnwire, zpay32), lightning-onion, go-lnurl, gofpdf, pdfcpu, gorm with SQLite, gRPC.

Muun.bitcoin_library_not_counted: btcd and lnd, as Go modules. Copies inside libwallet (btcsuitew, musig2v040) are counted

prebuilt.text: Rust zero-knowledge proof verifier (plonky2) linked as the static library multi-apple-ios-librs.a, built by libwallet/librs/makelibs.sh and not in the tree; FirebaseAnalytics and GoogleAppMeasurement xcframeworks from dl.google.com

Muun.patched: Go 1.24.7 toolchain is patched for cgo struct alignment (falcon/0001-align-to-ptrsize.patch); golang.org/x/mobile is replaced by the muun/mobile fork (libwallet/go.mod:200)

Phoenix.built_with: Swift (SwiftUI) over Kotlin Multiplatform shared code

engine.text: lightning-kmp {version:lightning-kmp} (Kotlin Multiplatform): Electrum client, swap-in wallet and final (BIP84) wallet

chain_data.text: An Electrum server picked at random from a built-in list of 15, trusted as given; the person can enter their own server in Settings

third_party.text: ACINQ co-signs swap-in deposits (MuSig2 2-of-2) until a refund delay of about six months, and is the channel peer for every on-chain send. The final wallet is the person's alone

libraries.text: bitcoin-kmp with secp256k1-kmp, Ktor, kotlinx-serialization, SQLDelight (Kotlin side); Firebase Messaging and a few small SwiftUI packages (Swift side)

prebuilt.text: Kotlin libraries (lightning-kmp, bitcoin-kmp, secp256k1-kmp native code, Ktor, SQLDelight) as compiled klibs from Maven Central; Firebase through Swift Package Manager

engine.text: LDK Node {version:synonym-ldk-node} (Synonym's fork, Rust); its on-chain wallet is BDK

chain_data.text: Synonym's Electrum server (bitkit.to); the person can change it in Settings > Advanced > Electrum Server

libraries.text: LDK Node (with BDK), bitkit-core, Paykit, VSS client, Lottie, swift-secp256k1

prebuilt.text: LDK Node, bitkit-core, Paykit and the VSS client, as XCFrameworks

engine.text: Embedded LND {version:lnd-blixt} (Go); the on-chain wallet is btcwallet, run in-process through react-native-turbo-lnd

chain_data.text: Neutrino (BIP157/158) through six default peers, four run by Blixt; the person can change the peers in Settings

libraries.text: React Native, react-native-turbo-lnd, @bufbuild/protobuf, secp256k1, bech32, react-native-nitro-tor, react-native-keychain, easy-peasy

prebuilt.text: Lndmobile.xcframework (LND), downloaded from the react-native-turbo-lnd release for the pinned LND commit

Blixt.patched: None in the app (no patch files); LND is Blixt's own fork (hsjoberg/lnd) with an added gossip speedloader

Zeus.built_with: React Native (TypeScript) with native modules and prebuilt Go and Rust libraries

engine.text: Embedded LND {version:lnd-zeus} (Go, Zeus's fork); the on-chain wallet is btcwallet. LDK Node (BDK) is an option, and remote nodes can be driven too

chain_data.text: Neutrino (BIP157/158) through five default peers, two run by Olympus; the person can add peers or allow only their own. The LDK Node option uses an Esplora server

third_party.text: Nobody for on-chain funds; they sit in the embedded wallet under one key on the phone

libraries.text: React Native, bitcoinjs-lib, noble and scure cryptography, bc-ur registries (Keystone, NGRAVE), Nostr (NDK), react-native-nitro-tor, Cashu CDK
libraries.cite: zeus:package.json:53; zeus:package.json:55; zeus:package.json:56; zeus:package.json:59; zeus:package.json:77; zeus:package.json:86; zeus:package.json:117; zeus:package.json:148

Zeus.bitcoin_library_not_counted: btcwallet (with btcd, neutrino) under LND; bitcoinjs-lib; BDK in the optional LDK Node

prebuilt.text: Lndmobile.xcframework (LND), LDKNodeFFI.xcframework (LDK Node), and the Cashu CDK and restore xcframeworks, downloaded from release archives pinned by SHA-256

Zeus.patched: Six postinstall scripts rewrite installed npm packages (two are Android-only: jcenter and notifications; four reach iOS: NativeEventEmitter, keychain cloudSync, noble-hashes exports, reanimated C++); rn-nodeify shims crypto, stream and dgram

not_compared: are widely used iPhone wallets whose apps are closed source, so there is no code to measure or cite.
Envoy, Bull Bitcoin, Bitcoin Keeper, Cake Wallet and Edge
publish source code and may be added. Each needs a measured iPhone build and a hand review of its features.
